name: Keyboard Chaos
summary: 键帽分拣整理模拟，2026 年 10 月 14 日上架，LostPixel 开发并发行，分类为休闲／独立／模拟，要把散落的 2692 枚键帽归位到 32 把键盘上。商店 AI 披露说开发期间用 AI 协助头脑风暴、开发与内容打磨，最终内容全部由团队审核整合，并声明游玩过程中不会实时生成 AI 内容。这三处用词都没有点名任何素材门类，所以八个领域全部登记为未说明，并标记范围未说明；那句运行时声明作为开发者自述在 ingame 条目下留档。讨论区与玩家评测里有多人声称玩法素材由 AI 生成、并认为披露有误导，属玩家自述，本站不据此定案。所有结论只有相关方自述支撑，未经独立审计。

sources.label: AI use in game
sources.excerpt:
I am struggling to find a way to contact the Lost Pixel team, but I had wishlisted this game a few weeks ago and was looking forward to playing it, only to find out that many of the gameplay elements were generated with AI. I am disappointed and will not be purchasing the game, but I do want to encourage the team to remake the game without relying on AI and I want to encourage consumers to be weary of AI-heavy games and products, especially in the "cozy" genre. AI is something that consumers are weary of and it can absolutely damage the reputation of indie game developers.
Krysanthe View Profile View Posts 1 1 1 Oct 9 @ 11:53am Report this post In the same light some people just don't care about AI. I personally don't care and buy nearly all the tidy up games that come out AI or not. Doesn't matter to me at all. I am not saying this to debate you as everyone is allowed to have their own opinion and I am not trying to change yours. Just figured you are taking a stand and I would say you aren't speaking for everyone. I would rather they keep the game the way it is as it looks great so far. #1
TsukasaWM View Profile View Posts 1 1 Oct 14 @ 4:52pm Report this post Can we have just 1 single game where people don't come in and whine and virtue signal about AI use already. I swear do you guys just sit in the new game queue so you can be the first to rush in complain about it #2
Llamawolfe View Profile View Posts 1 1 Oct 14 @ 5:58pm Report this post Originally posted by TsukasaWM : Can we have just 1 single game where people don't come in and whine and virtue signal about AI use already. I swear do you guys just sit in the new game queue so you can be the first to rush in complain about it I'm almost positive that is what people do. Within 10 minutes after a game launches there is a post on every single indie game complaining about AI usage. It even happens on games that specifically say they don't use AI on their store page. I'm tired of seeing it. AI isn't going anywhere and it's going to be used more and more often. These people just need to get over it already. #3
Requiem View Profile View Posts 1 1 Oct 15 @ 7:06am Report this post AI is not going away, AI helps speed up manual coding, people who are against AI have NO clue how difficult it actually can be or how frustrating it can be to actually work with AI tools, its not just prompting chatgtp or whatever " make me a game" Human input and brains and human artistic view is always needed to eventually create something the HUMAN had in his/her vision. but i know its useless to explain this to those that simple want to hate on AI, for the reasons they have no clue, its like convincing flat earthers that the earth is not flat :D so yeah i embrace AI as a "tool" and the great stuff it can "HELP" build. it still helps if you know some coding, or skills yes, but basically, IS a game fun? if the answer is yes, it should not matter how it came to be. haters gonna hate. and hate is nothing more then fearing the unknown, lacking the knowledge of AI, and just see it as " they steal stuff, they make real artist go out of a job!" nope, some REAL artist play it smart and use their knowledge to better work with AI as an assisting "TOOL" and efficiently working with AI? for that is an ART by itself. #4
Kimari View Profile View Posts Oct 16 @ 1:03pm Report this post Game is apparently making an inaccurate reference images to follow that have keys that don't exist but sure, AI a fantastic tool that improves the experience. Brains gone #5
TheChaosGoddess View Profile View Posts 2 Oct 17 @ 4:18pm Report this post Another thing about AI, I also get the struggle artist are having with AI, I know people who are artist for a living and how much it has affected their business, but the people who come in and harp on having AI images and belittle the devs for not hiring real artist have obviously NEVER hired a real artist to make anything. It's friggin expensive and I'm speaking from first hand experience having had to hire someone to make some things for me. When you're a solo dev, or a very tiny team, money doesn't grow on trees to pay for the creation of their game, and frankly, I don't think that they should be held back or penalized for fulfilling a dream on making games by using it bc they couldn't afford to pay someone for art in a game, but at the same time they also didn't want the same resource pack that we are frankly all getting really really tired of seeing. #6
Slyty View Profile View Posts Oct 18 @ 12:44am Report this post So, to "encourage the team to remake the game without relying on AI" while also "will not be purchasing the game" you're literally telling them to invest and go bakrupt on the project because spacegecko17 has some vertue problem to exhibit ? Bro I'm myself a graphic designer, that's freaking expensive, if they decide someday to do a game without ai it will be with money, yknow ? #7
Massive Dynamic View Profile View Posts Oct 20 @ 4:25am Report this post At least OP has had the stones to post on their proper account. Most of these "AI bad - will not buy" posts come from obvious second accounts (Steam level 0 - no games in library etc,) and you just know that their actual account is probably brimming with tidy-up games full of "slop". At the end of the day - you want your tidy-up game to cost under a fiver? Then you're probably going to have to accept a certain amount of AI use. It costs money to list a game on Steam and they take a significant cut of each sale too but the Anti-Ai mob don't take this into consideration. I'm sure they have visions of an artist starving in a garret while the developer of Tidy-up the Latest Thing is rolling around on a bed covered in Benjamins. It's just not the case. Having said all that, Kimari has a point - if keyboards are showing keys that don't exist in reality then something needs to be done and the fact that nothing was done before release show that these particular devs DGAF. The devs of all the tidy-up games I buy are usually bending over backwards to fix issues and problems and that's why I bought their game in the first place - I check the discussion board before making a decision and if a dev shows that they care about their game and are making sure it's the best it can be, then I can forgive a bit of AI. #8
Hashtag Heathen View Profile View Posts Oct 22 @ 2:22pm Report this post Originally posted by TsukasaWM : Can we have just 1 single game where people don't come in and whine and virtue signal about AI use already. I swear do you guys just sit in the new game queue so you can be the first to rush in complain about it THIS!!!! I was discussing this when it came to small, indie developers, & in the game people were yeling about, if each image costed $20 (which is on the low end), then they would've had to fork over about $10,000!!! So these people who virtue signal about AI use are basically saying that they do NOT want indie devs from actually being able to make great games!!! There are bigger fish to fry, & personally, I'd rather that I get to enjoy a game that is great & see small indie devs grow, than just no longer having indie devs publish... sources.excerpt: I was looking forward to this game so much, but the AI Disclosure section feels extremely misleading.

reviewNote: 核查英文商店页完整 AI 披露栏、身份（开发与发行均为 LostPixel，正式版）与英文讨论区首页（可见 15 个主题、总数 21，仅覆盖首页）。首页命中关键词的主题 AI use in game 已完整读取正文与全部 9 条可见回复：楼主说自己原本在愿望单里，得知许多玩法元素由 AI 生成后决定不买，并劝开发者重制；回帖以玩家立场分成两派，有人表示不在意、有人抱怨新游戏发布十分钟就涌进 AI 投诉帖，还有玩家指出参照图里出现了现实中不存在的按键。帖内没有任何开发者发言，作者身份也未与官方账号绑定核实，因此全部内容按玩家自述处理，不改变任何领域结论。公开报道单独检索 1 次（原始响应存档 press-search.json，4 条结果），登记并读取 1 条来源：gamemoki.com 的本作页面，它转录了 Steam 上的玩家评测，其中一篇写道披露部分极具误导性；该站为评测聚合方，转录内容仍是玩家自述。其余结果为商店页，已有官方取证。本作是披露措辞宽泛、社区争议明显的典型：范围未说明的标记与玩家分歧一并写在页面上。
disclosureQuote: AI tools were used during the development of this game to assist with brainstorming, development, and content refinement. All final content was reviewed and integrated by the development team. The game does not generate AI content in real time during gameplay.
disclosureQuoteNote: Steam 商店 AI 生成内容披露栏完整原文，2026-11-05 核查；可能随商店页更新。

english.summary: A keycap sorting and assembling sim released on Oct 14, 2026, developed and published by LostPixel and filed under Casual, Indie and Simulation, where 2692 loose keycaps have to be matched back onto 32 keyboards. The Steam AI disclosure says AI tools assisted brainstorming, development and content refinement during development, that all final content was reviewed and integrated by the team, and that the game does not generate AI content in real time during gameplay. None of those clauses names a specific content discipline, so all eight areas are recorded as not addressed and the scope is flagged as unspecified, with the run-time sentence kept on record under the ingame entry. Several forum threads and player reviews claim gameplay assets were AI generated and call the disclosure misleading; those are player statements and are not used to settle any area. Every finding rests on what the parties involved say about their own work and none of it has been independently audited.
english.reviewNote: Checked the complete English Steam AI disclosure block, the identity (LostPixel as both developer and publisher, a full release rather than a demo) and the English discussion homepage, which shows 15 visible topics out of 21 and covers only that first page. The homepage topic that matches the keyword, AI use in game, was read in full together with all 9 visible replies: the original poster says the game was on their wishlist until they learned that many gameplay elements were generated with AI and that they will not buy it, while the replies split between players who do not care, players annoyed that every new indie release draws AI complaints within ten minutes, and one player noting that reference images show keys that do not exist on real keyboards. No developer posts appear in that thread and no poster identity is bound to an official account, so the whole thread is treated as player testimony and changes no area finding. One dedicated web search was run, archived as press-search.json, whose 4 results are each dispositioned; one source was registered and read in full, the gamemoki.com page for this game, which transcribes Steam player reviews including one that calls the AI disclosure section extremely misleading. That aggregator only mirrors what players wrote, so it carries the same self-statement limit. The other results were Steam pages already covered by the official evidence.
